title: Covariance with a Boolean junta
statement: Let $n,k$ be nonnegative integers, and let $f:\\{-1,1\\}^n\\to\\mathbb R$ be Fourier-regular at level $k$ with bound $\\varepsilon\\ge0$. If $h:\\{-1,1\\}^n\\to\\{-1,1\\}$ depends on at most $k$ coordinates, then $\\operatorname{Cov}(f,h)\\le 2^{k/2}\\varepsilon$, with covariance taken under the uniform measure on the cube.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is Fourier-regular at level $k$ with bound $\\varepsilon$
$h$ is a Boolean-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
